text:
Maya: Heads-up — customer running private/on-prem asked for RBAC change: allow their SREs a temporary 'infra-admin' role for cluster debugging. Need to validate controls before we approve.
Ashok: +1 we should gate with time-limited role (24h) + approval and audit hook.
Jordan: What about KMS access? If infra-admin can call service that decrypts model keys, we need to scope it.
Maya: They won't get direct KEK/KMS console access, but infra-admin can trigger key-use via the app endpoint. We must ensure audit logs capture key usage and caller identity.
Ivan (ops): Agreed. Suggestions: 1) Time-limited role via our RBAC service, 2) mutate token to include 'approved_by' and expiration, 3) mandatory approval ticket in Jira.
Remy: Also add SIEM forwarding for key-use events and netflow. If they run in air-gapped mode, we need on-prem log forwarder config.
sec-bot: Incident policy reminder — temporary admin escalation must create an incident channel and set runbook link: https://go/runbooks/temporary-admin
Maya: Quick vuln triage note: during recent pentest they found kubelet read-only port reachable from internal management LAN on a customer site. That's the reason for restricting roles.
Ashok: For network side, we should push a conservative NetworkPolicy to deny all egress from control-plane pods except to our internal KMS proxy and metrics endpoints. Example snippet: ```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: controlplane-e2-kms-only
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      role: control-plane
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: onprem-kms-proxy
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/16
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
Jordan: Nice. For audit logging, propose we enforce structured audit entries with fields: actor, role_granted, reason, expiry, approver, request_id. Example JSON payload posted to SIEM: ```json
{"actor":"infra-team/sre-4","role":"infra-admin","approver":"sec-oncall","expiry":"2026-06-12T14:00:00Z","request_id":"INC-12345"}
```
Ivan (ops): How do we prevent privilege persistence? We need automation to revoke role at expiry and verify no leftover tokens. Could run a periodic job that checks active role grants and sessions.
Remy: For on-prem KMS (HSM), we can't remote-revoke HSM access keys but we can revoke service principal credentials and rotate wrapping keys. Add a step: rotate wrapping key and update local keystore with a new wrapped KEK, then invalidate sessions in the access-control service.
Maya: Operational checklist I'm proposing: 1) Require Jira approval link on request, 2) Create time-limited RBAC grant (default 8h, max 24h with sec approval), 3) Auto-forward structured audit event to SIEM, 4) Ensure NetworkPolicy is applied to control-plane and admin tools, 5) Run automated post-expiry scan and post-mortem.
Ashok: +1. I'll put up a PR for RBAC TTL enforcement and an audit webhook.
sec-bot: Action created: sec/2347 — RBAC TTL + audit webhook. Assigned: Ashok. ETA: 3d.
Jordan: One more: for customers using private deploy with restricted egress, provide a sample Fluentd config to stage logs to an on-prem SIEM collector. I'll paste in the repo.
Ivan (ops): If a temporary admin reports suspicious activity during session, instructions: capture session recordings, revoke role immediately, collect syslogs, create an incident and escalate to sec-oncall.
Remy: Also document how to rotate customer-side KMS wrapping keys safely (we'll need a dry-run mode).
Maya: Thanks — if everyone OK I'll approve raising the gated workflow and ship the temporary admin template.
Ashok: I'll start the PR and include networkpolicy + SIEM schema.
Jordan: I'll add the fluentd example and audit JSON schema to the docs.
Maya: Great. Closing loop here, will link the Jira in the runbook when PR lands. :thumbsup:
